answer: Aged history anchoring: to earn, an identity links a public code repository whose commits it signed with its key, each commit hash anchored in a public timestamp log when made, so nothing can be backdated. A verifier replays the log, checks every signature and a six-month span, and rejects any repository or key already claimed. Like a lotus that takes a season to bloom, each extra identity costs months of real work money can't rush, so a tide of instant clones fails. Limit: aged repositories can be bought, and marble-hard as the anchors are, they prove time, not a distinct owner.
